reviewer_evidence: Independently inspected each source statement and all four localized explanations, including original battery and oil-can images under data/source/images; the figures match their cited meanings. Ford https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/catalog/owner_guides/96mysog1e.pdf printed 57–59 distinguishes charge and oil pressure lamps, stopping safely and shutting off for oil pressure; MAHLE https://workshop-heroes.mahle.com/en/article/running-smoothly supports oil pump and maintenance-deposit relationship. 30607 accurately retains possible indirect chain and printed answer.

30611/30612: https://asset.moto.it/download/b3e08491d33079f2e6d71dce639fe696/patente-c-1.pdf printed steering notes merely repeat quiz claim. Haldex https://www.haldex.com/globalassets/north-america/documents/power-steering/l20696 links excessive flow to road wander/over-steering; this is a steering-response example, not by itself demonstration of the claimed vehicle-dynamics oversteer/understeer mechanism.

Re-reviewed revised 30611/30612 all languages: Haldex steering guide p.1 documents excess-flow-associated over-steering/road wander; TRW steering diagnostics discusses gear adjustment and abnormal responses. These do not prove the exact under/oversteer relationship alleged by the quiz. Learner copy preserves VERO, explicitly discloses unresolved causal link, and does not equate excessive/abnormal steering response with tyre-related dynamics. No positive proof of the 30612 mechanism was found; accepted as a transparent source-qualified explanation, not a proven verdict. Other rows unchanged from full review.

issues.reason: The official item states that failure to change oil at the scheduled interval can cause the oil-pressure warning and marks it FALSO. The technical sources describe an indirect possible chain from irregular oil changes to deposits and from sludge or deposits to low oil pressure. It is unclear whether the quiz intends only the missed date as a direct trigger or excludes this possible indirect cause; the printed verdict cannot safely be reconciled without adjudication.

issues.reason: The only cited Patente C notes repeat the quiz assertion but do not independently establish how incorrect power-steering adjustment causes vehicle-dynamics oversteer. Haldex documents possible excessive steering response/wander, which is not itself proof of rear-tyre grip loss or cornering oversteer. Supply technical evidence or qualify the uncertainty to learners.

The cited Patente C notes merely repeat the source assertion; no independent technical mechanism shows incorrect power-steering adjustment causes vehicle-dynamics understeer. Supply direct support or qualify the uncertainty, distinguishing inadequate steering response from front-tyre grip loss.

reviewer_evidence: Independently inspected each source statement and all four localized explanations, including original battery and oil-can images under data/source/images; the figures match their cited meanings. Ford https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/catalog/owner_guides/96mysog1e.pdf printed 57–59 distinguishes charge and oil pressure lamps, stopping safely and shutting off for oil pressure; MAHLE https://workshop-heroes.mahle.com/en/article/running-smoothly supports oil pump and maintenance-deposit relationship. 30607 accurately retains possible indirect chain and printed answer.

30611/30612: https://asset.moto.it/download/b3e08491d33079f2e6d71dce639fe696/patente-c-1.pdf printed steering notes merely repeat quiz claim. Haldex https://www.haldex.com/globalassets/north-america/documents/power-steering/l20696 links excessive flow to road wander/over-steering; this is a steering-response example, not by itself demonstration of the claimed vehicle-dynamics oversteer/understeer mechanism.
